purpose: How many ways can different people fill different roles?
meaning: Multiply the available choices for successive labeled roles: n, then n−1, continuing for r factors. The empty product for zero roles is one.

definition.setting: Choose distinct volunteers for r different labeled roles from n available people. A person can fill at most one role, and swapping two people changes the assignment.

signature.r: Number of different labeled roles to fill.
signature.P(n,r): Number of ordered role assignments without repetition.

conditions: Whole counts satisfy 0 ≤ r ≤ n ≤ 8. Zero roles have one empty assignment. No repetition, ties, circular equivalence or probability model is included.
All chosen inputs are whole numbers in the declared finite ranges. Both views and the story use the same evaluated state.

properties.conditions: Whole counts satisfy 0 ≤ r ≤ n ≤ 8. Zero roles have one empty assignment. No repetition, ties, circular equivalence or probability model is included.
properties.derivation: The first role has n choices; each later role excludes those already used. Multiplying r branch counts gives n!/(n−r)! for the stated domain.
